contracts.source: Infineon press release: Infineon signs 200-millimeter silicon carbide wafer supply (10-15-2026)
contracts.signal: Infineon and Wolfspeed signed a new multi-year supply agreement for 200-millimeter silicon carbide (SiC) wafers, transitioning Infineon's existing Wolfspeed supply relationship from 150-millimeter to 200-millimeter substrate technology; the agreement directly supports Infineon's conversion to 200-millimeter SiC manufacturing. Infineon COO Alexander Gorski: the agreement 'further broadens our strong supply base for our 200-millimeter high-volume manufacturing, building on a 20-year supply relationship between our two companies.'

players.product: OptiMOS MOSFETs, SiC modules, gate drivers

quarterly_data.quarter: Infineon press release: Infineon signs 200-millimeter silicon carbide wafer supply (10-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Infineon says it is converting its silicon carbide manufacturing from 150-millimeter to 200-millimeter and operates a multi-source SiC substrate strategy to maintain supply chain flexibility and quality across its global manufacturing network, including its 200-millimeter SiC fab in Kulim, Malaysia, which the company says is designed to be the world's largest and most competitive silicon carbide manufacturing facility. The company says AI datacenters are beginning to emerge as a significant demand driver for SiC power semiconductors, alongside growing SiC adoption across electric vehicle drivetrains, solar inverters and industrial motor drives.
